Title: ​Early recognition and appropriate treatment of surgical problems in children is crucial for a successful outcome

NewsContent:
​"Many of the surgical conditions of childhood are different from those of the adult and are approached from a different view point. Children are not small adults, the working of their body, the way they respond to illness and their disease pattern 'is unique and different from that of adults" said Dr Zafar Nazir, Assistant Professor of Pediatric Surgery and Consultant Pediatric Surgeon at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving the presentation on "Surgery in Children" at 'Signs, Symptoms and Care' a monthly health awareness programme held on October 28. 2000. 
 
Dr Zalar Nazir explained,"When your child needs medical treatment, you want him or her to be seen by a Pediatrician. A doctor who specializes in diseases of children. So if your child needs an operation, you will want to consult a surgeon who is qualified and experienced in operating on children called 'Pediatric Surgeon".
 
Dr Zafar Nazir said,"Pediatric surgeons utilize their expertise in providing care for most of the surgical problems mainly circumcision. Hernia repair, acute appendicitis, obstruction in the intestine, etc. In addition, the) have particular expertise in Neonatal (newborn) surgery prenatal (before birth) diagnosis and counseling, trauma, cancer in children, surgery of kidney and bladder".
 
Dr Zafar azir stressed, “Pediatric surgeons specialize in the surgical care of children. They are surgeons who by training are oriented towards working with children and understanding their special medical and social needs. In addition they work with various specialists to provide best care to their patients. They are able to save whole life times. And have the opportunity to follow their patients through a productive young life into adulthood".
 
 Another speaker Dr M. Arif Mateen Khan, Assistant Professor of Pediatric Surgery and Consultant Pediatric Surgeon at AK U H, elaborated by saying,"the new born period is a time of rapid maturation, adaptation and dependency, which presents a special challenge to the surgeon caring for the new born infants".
 
Dr Arif Mateen emphasized on early recognition and management of common surgical conditions affecting the infant and newborns, through a form of 'continuing surgical education directed at the community, Intestinal obstruction is the most common abdominal emergency in neonates and occurs in about 1/2000 live births.
 
He further outlined the principles of successful management of neonates with suspected obstruction by recognizing the condition early, institute appropriate investigation, assure complete preoperative resuscitation and perform surgical procedure for the underlying condition.
 
The panelists, who included Dr Shabbir Hussain and Dr Muhammad Arshad answered questions for the audience at the end of the program.
